title: Reducing Alcohol-Involved Suicidal Ideation and Behavior
official: Reducing Alcohol-Involved Suicidal Ideation and Behavior
summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether a brief skills training can help people cope better with distress and reduce suicidal thoughts and behaviors that happen along with alcohol use. The study looks at this both in a lab and in everyday life. It is for adults ages 21 to 54 who currently have thoughts of suicide and who engage in heavy episodic drinking (drinking a large amount of alcohol on a single occasion; specifically, 4 drinks in 2 hours for females and 5 drinks in 2 hours for males).

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Can two coping skills from Dialectical Behavior Therapy (paced breathing and expanding awareness) reduce distress, suicidal thoughts, and urges to self-harm while a person has been drinking alcohol?
* Can text messages sent during the two weeks after the lab visit help people who drink alcohol have fewer suicidal thoughts and behaviors, compared with getting no text messages?
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Ages 21 to 54
* Suicidal ideation at least once in the past month;
* Heavy episodic drinking at least once in the past month

Exclusion Criteria:

* Any medical contraindications to alcohol use
* Past-month opioid use
* Pregnant
* Have had a psychotic episode in the past month
* Are in or seeking treatment for an alcohol use disorder
* Have not consumed the amount of alcohol in the past month that would be administered during the proximal change experiment
